\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newcommand{\term}[1]{#1}
\begin{document}
Letters right after inline math stay on the line of the math, as in the
$i$th row, the $n$th and $(n+1)$st terms, and a gap of $-4$pt. So do
the letters after math that follows a no-break space, as in the~$k$th
entry.

\begin{theorem}The $i$th row is zero.\end{theorem}

So is \emph{the $n$th term} of the sequence, and the last
entry.\footnote{See the $k$th entry.}

So do the characters right before and after the math up to the next
space, as in an $n$-dimensional space, the $n$\`eme terme, the vector
($x$, $y$), and $x$'s value.

\begin{theorem}For all~$x$~and so on.\end{theorem}
And a tie in a footnote.\footnote{See Lemma~$2$ and $3$.}

A box or a term right after the math stays whole: the $i$\fbox{th row},
the $j$\framebox[3cm][l]{two words}, and the $m$\term{th power} of it.
\end{document}
